definitions: A village and civil parish in the Mid Sussex District of West Sussex, England.
A historic English noble family, prominent from the 13th to the 15th centuries.
Sir Edward Poynings (1459–1521), an English soldier, administrator, and diplomat, best known for 'Poynings' Law' in Ireland.
examples: Poynings is nestled at the foot of the South Downs.
The Poynings family held significant lands in Sussex.
Poynings' Law greatly impacted Irish governance.
